transcript.text: I understand this is worrying. A tumble dryer that truly 'won't stop' usually points to one of two things: either the control system (the board or timer) has a stuck relay keeping power on, or the start switch itself is jammed mechanically. Before we look at parts, let's narrow it down with two quick checks: 1. The Power Reset: Switch the dryer off at the wall socket and leave it for 2 minutes. Plug it back in, close the door firmly, select a standard programme, and press start. Does it now stop when you press 'stop' or end the cycle normally? If yes, it was likely a temporary electronic glitch. 2. The Symptom Check: If it still runs continuously even after pressing stop (and only stops if you unplug it), please tell me exactly what is happening while it runs. Is the drum turning and the heater on? Or is it just tumbling without heat? Please let me know the result of the reset first, as that often clears simple electronic locks.
it finishes and says End but then the drum keeps turning every couple of minutes. stops if I open the door. no heat, clothes are cool

Thanks for that detail. The fact that it says 'End' but keeps tumbling intermittently suggests the control system isn't cutting power to the drum motor correctly once the timer reaches zero. This is often a fault with the main control board (the relay sticking on) or, less commonly, the door switch logic. Before we look at hardware faults, I need to rule out a programme setting that mimics this behaviour:
1. Please confirm exactly which programme you selected before pressing start (e.g., Cottons, Synthetics, Delicates, etc.).
2. Also, is there any option on the display like 'Anti-crease', 'Refresh', or 'Cool Down' active? Some programmes pause and tumble intermittently at the end to prevent creasing. If it was a standard drying programme (like Cottons) and no anti-crease mode was selected, then this is likely an electrical fault with the control board.
I don't remember which programme I picked, sorry. I don't know what anti-crease means. I have the manual though.

This sounds exactly like the normal 'anti-crease' or 'cool down' phase. Most tumble dryers are designed to keep the drum turning occasionally for 20–60 minutes after the programme ends to stop your clothes from creasing while they cool. The fact that it stops immediately when you open the door suggests this is a safety feature, not a fault. You do not need to do anything. If you prefer, just leave the door slightly ajar (prop it with a towel) once the cycle finishes; this usually tells the dryer to stop tumbling sooner because it detects the door is open. If the drum continues to turn for more than an hour after 'End', or if it starts heating up again during these pauses, then please let me know and we can look at the control board.

candidates: Control board or timer fault (stuck relay) (high)
Start switch stuck in the 'on' position (medium)
Programme setting or child lock confusion (low)
